label: N1QL() call result iterator
type: the streamed cursor object returned by an inline SQL++ statement or an eventing:n1ql-function-call from inside a handler. Object of the already-promoted requiresExplicitClose - the handler must call .close() on it to free resources, since it is a streamed cursor and not a materialized array.
evidence: results.close();              // End the query and free resources held
note: NOT ALWAYS CLOSED IN THE DOCS' OWN EXAMPLES. basicN1qlSelectStmt/basicN1qlPreparedSelectStmt/advancedSelfRecursion all call .close() correctly; docControlledSelfExpiry.md calls N1QL(stmt) and never captures or closes a return value at all. Plausibly a legitimate fire-and-forget-DML exception (no rows to iterate on a bare UPDATE), but the docs never say so, and the page sits in the same batch as three pages that DO close it - flagged in docs-issues/server-eventing-n1ql-result-not-closed-one-page.
relates_to_competency_question: Does an inline N1QL() call in a handler leak resources if the handler forgets to close it, and does every worked example actually close it?
